search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Salmonella cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and outbreak details in the United States during May–July 2024, covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, subnational locations, and dates reported.
search_reasoning: The upstream planned queries are structurally sound but have two weaknesses: (1) they use rigid quoted phrase strings (e.g., "Salmonella outbreak United States 2024") that may miss CDC outbreak investigation pages, FDA food-safety recalls, and state health department advisories that use different phrasing; (2) the 10-query inventory exceeds the 4-query-per-iteration cap, so we must prioritize the highest-yield query types for iteration 1. Priority order: (a) CDC official outbreak investigation pages are the single most authoritative source for confirmed US Salmonella case counts and are best reached via a targeted web_search against cdc.gov; (b) FDA outbreak/recall pages often carry case counts and hospitalization data for foodborne Salmonella; (c) ProMED/PAHO/WHO situation reports provide international validation and may cite US figures; (d) news aggregation (e.g., outbreak news) surfaces state-level detail and hospitalization data not yet in CDC summaries. We refine query text to remove over-restrictive quoted phrases, add CDC/FDA agency signals, and include the specific date window terms "May 2024", "June 2024", "July 2024" to improve temporal precision. We stay within the 4-query cap for iteration 1 and reserve literature/database queries for iteration 2 if gaps remain.

query_batch.query: CDC Salmonella outbreak investigation 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths site:cdc.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC's outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative source for confirmed US Salmonella case counts, hospitalization rates, death counts, and subnational location breakdowns. Restricting to cdc.gov maximises precision. Removing rigid quoted phrases allows the query to match CDC's own page titles (e.g., 'Outbreak Investigation of Salmonella: [Vehicle] (Month Year)').
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation summary pages listing case counts, illness onset dates, states affected, hospitalizations, and deaths
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; CDC outbreak investigation branding; epidemiologic curve or case-count table

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak United States cases hospitalizations 2024 May June July site:cdc.gov OR site:fda.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Extends coverage to FDA, which publishes foodborne illness outbreak advisories and recall notices that include Salmonella case counts and hospitalization data linked to specific food vehicles and states. The OR operator captures both agencies in one query slot, maximising yield within the 4-query cap.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory or recall notice citing Salmonella case counts, states affected, and illness dates; CDC multistate outbreak page
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov or cdc.gov domain; official outbreak advisory or recall notice language; case count and hospitalization figures

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations state health department
query_batch.query_rationale: State health departments (e.g., CDPH, NYSDOH, TXDSHS) often publish their own Salmonella outbreak advisories with subnational case counts, locality detail, and hospitalization figures before CDC finalises a multistate summary. A broad web search without domain restriction surfaces these state-level pages, which are critical for the subnational_location and locality target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State health department press release or outbreak advisory with case counts, county or city breakdown, and illness date range
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domain (e.g., health.state.xx.us or dph.xx.gov); official press release or advisory language; epidemiologic data table

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak US 2024 cases deaths recalled food ProMED OR "outbreak news" OR "food safety news"
query_batch.query_rationale: ProMED-mail and specialist food-safety news outlets (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today) aggregate and cite official case counts, hospitalization data, and death figures for US Salmonella outbreaks, often with state-level granularity and earlier publication dates than CDC final summaries. This query covers the news/situation-report source type and may surface outbreaks not yet finalised on CDC pages.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: ProMED post or food-safety news article citing official case counts, states affected, hospitalization numbers, and death toll for a specific Salmonella outbreak event
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: ProMED archive post with DONs reference; Food Safety News or Outbreak News Today byline citing CDC or state health department figures; publication date within May–July 2024

expected_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation summary with case count, illness onset date range, states affected, hospitalization count, and death count
FDA outbreak advisory or recall notice with Salmonella case counts and state distribution
State health department press release with subnational case counts and locality detail
ProMED or food-safety news article citing official figures for a US Salmonella outbreak event in May–July 2024
Epidemiologic curve or case-count table with confirmed/probable/suspected breakdown
Evidence quotes containing numeric case counts, hospitalization rates, or death figures attributable to Salmonella within the time window
expected_source_characteristics: Official US federal public health agency page (CDC, FDA) with outbreak investigation branding
State or territorial health department page on a .gov domain
International disease surveillance aggregator (ProMED-mail) with post date in 2024
Specialist food-safety journalism outlet citing primary official sources
Pages containing structured epidemiologic data: case counts, dates, locations, hospitalization and death figures
language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. The United States is an English-language jurisdiction; CDC, FDA, and state health departments publish exclusively in English for official outbreak data. No localization to other languages is required for this task. Spanish-language sources (e.g., from Puerto Rico's Departamento de Salud) could be relevant for subnational coverage of US territories but are deferred to iteration 2 if territorial data is needed.
trust_considerations: Prefer cdc.gov and fda.gov pages as primary authoritative sources for confirmed case counts and deaths
State .gov health department pages are authoritative for subnational data but may use different case definitions
ProMED and Food Safety News are acceptable secondary sources when they directly cite and quote official figures
Avoid sources that do not cite a primary official agency or that aggregate without attribution
Check that reported dates fall within 2024-05-01–2024-07-31; CDC pages may report outbreaks that started earlier but were active in the window
Be alert to the distinction between 'confirmed' and 'total' (confirmed + probable) case counts, which CDC sometimes conflates in summary language
stop_condition_hypothesis: Coverage is sufficient when at least one CDC outbreak investigation page, one FDA advisory or recall notice, and one news/situation-report source are identified that together provide case counts, hospitalization figures, at least one death figure or explicit zero, subnational location(s), and a date reported within the 2024-05-01–2024-07-31 window. If iteration 1 returns these, iteration 2 can be scoped to fill remaining field gaps (e.g., probable/suspected breakdowns, state-level granularity).
warnings: Upstream queries used over-restrictive quoted phrases that may suppress relevant CDC and FDA pages with different title formats — refined in this iteration
The 10-query upstream inventory exceeds the 4-query-per-iteration cap; only the 4 highest-priority, highest-yield queries are included here
CDC outbreak investigation pages are sometimes published weeks after the outbreak window closes; pages dated after 2024-07-31 may still contain data for the target window
Some Salmonella outbreaks in this window may be linked to specific food vehicles (e.g., cucumbers, eggs, poultry) — food-vehicle terms can be added in iteration 2 if needed
State-level data may use 'probable' or 'suspected' case categories not present in CDC federal summaries — both source types needed for full field coverage

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong coverage of CDC outbreak investigation pages and some FDA/news sources, but several important gaps remain for the specific May–July 2024 window: (1) The most directly relevant outbreak — Backyard Poultry May 2024 — was found but its hospitalization and death counts are not visible in the snippet; the index/summary page (not just the investigation update) needs to be surfaced. (2) The Fresh Basil April 2024 outbreak snippet shows no case counts — it may have illness dates extending into May 2024. (3) No CDC outbreak pages specifically dated May, June, or July 2024 (other than Backyard Poultry) have been surfaced — there may be additional outbreaks (e.g., linked to cantaloupes, onions, or other vehicles) active in that window. (4) FDA recall/advisory pages for May–July 2024 Salmonella events have not been individually surfaced (only 3 fda.gov results appeared, none with visible case counts in snippets). (5) FSIS/USDA appeared once but without case-count detail. (6) State-level subnational data (cases_probable, cases_suspected, locality) is still absent. (7) The CDC 2024 multistate outbreak summary page was found but its per-outbreak breakdown for May–July needs targeted follow-up. Iteration 2 should: (a) target CDC outbreak index pages specifically for May–July 2024 vehicles not yet surfaced; (b) target FDA advisories with case counts for that window; (c) target Food Safety News and CIDRAP for state-level and hospitalization detail; (d) use the CDC 2024 summary page as a pivot to find individual outbreak pages active in the window.

query_batch.query: CDC Salmonella outbreak investigation June 2024 OR July 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths site:cdc.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Iteration 1 surfaced the Backyard Poultry May 2024 outbreak but no CDC investigation pages specifically initiated in June or July 2024. This query directly targets CDC outbreak pages for those two months, which are the most underrepresented part of the window. The CDC 2024 summary mentions 38 Salmonella outbreaks — individual pages for June–July events are the highest-priority gap.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation index or update page with title containing 'June 2024' or 'July 2024', listing case counts, states, hospitalizations, and deaths
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; outbreak investigation page URL pattern /salmonella/outbreaks/[vehicle]-06-24/ or -07-24/; Fast Facts box with case/hospitalization/death counts

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak 2024 cases hospitalizations "May 2024" OR "June 2024" OR "July 2024" site:cdc.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Complements iter2_q1 by using quoted month-year phrases to match CDC pages that mention illness onset dates or report dates in the May–July 2024 window, even if the outbreak was named for a different month. This is particularly important for outbreaks like the Eggs September 2024 event (illness onset May 23) and any other outbreaks where the vehicle was identified later but illnesses began in the window.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation page with illness onset dates or case-count update dates falling in May–July 2024; Fast Facts or investigation update table with numeric case/hospitalization/death data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; quoted date strings matching the target window; epidemiologic curve or case-count table

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak United States May June July 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths FDA advisory recall site:fda.gov OR site:fsis.usda.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Iteration 1 returned only 3 fda.gov results and 1 fsis.usda.gov result, none with visible case counts in snippets. FDA outbreak advisories and FSIS public health alerts for Salmonella events in May–July 2024 are critical secondary authoritative sources that often include case counts, hospitalization figures, and state distributions not yet captured. FSIS covers meat/poultry Salmonella events specifically.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory or FSIS public health alert dated May–July 2024 with Salmonella case counts, states affected, and illness date range; recall notice linking to CDC case data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov or fsis.usda.gov domain; official outbreak advisory or public health alert language; case count and hospitalization figures; publication date May–July 2024

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations "state" "confirmed" "May" OR "June" OR "July" site:foodsafetynews.com OR site:cidrap.umn.edu OR site:outbreaknewstoday.com
query_batch.query_rationale: Food Safety News, CIDRAP, and Outbreak News Today are the highest-quality specialist news sources for US Salmonella outbreak coverage. They routinely publish state-level case breakdowns, hospitalization figures, and probable/suspected case counts that are absent from CDC federal summaries. CIDRAP appeared twice in iteration 1 but without visible case counts; targeting these domains directly with month-year terms maximises the chance of surfacing subnational data and filling the cases_probable/cases_suspected/locality gaps that remain entirely uncovered.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Food Safety News or CIDRAP article dated May–July 2024 citing official case counts by state, hospitalization numbers, and death figures for a specific Salmonella outbreak; Outbreak News Today post with state-level breakdown
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: foodsafetynews.com, cidrap.umn.edu, or outbreaknewstoday.com domain; article publication date May–July 2024; direct citation of CDC or state health department figures; numeric case/hospitalization/death data
